settingsVirtualPrinter.title: Virtual printer
settingsVirtualPrinter.description: A fake LAN printer your slicer can send to. The file lands in the queue, the review inbox or the library, or is proxied to a real printer. Only the first enabled virtual printer is served.
settingsVirtualPrinter.step1: Start the service: docker compose --profile virtual-printer up -d.
settingsVirtualPrinter.step2: Open Device, pick the printer by LAN and choose the virtual printer by name (or add it with the host IP + serial).
settingsVirtualPrinter.step3: Enter the access code above when asked, then use Print / Send as usual.

settingsSlicer.title: Slicer integration
settingsSlicer.description: Send sliced files straight from OrcaSlicer to your library.
settingsSlicer.tokensNote: Uses the same API tokens as the browser extension — a token from either works for both.
settingsSlicer.step1Body: OrcaSlicer → Process → Others → Post-processing scripts: python3 /path/to/slicer_postprocess.py, with INTAKE_URL (e.g. {{url}}) and INTAKE_TOKEN set in the script's environment. Every sliced plate is uploaded and matched to a model by name (or a new model is created).
settingsSlicer.step1Note: This path uploads plain .gcode — rich history and metadata, but not printable from this app.
settingsSlicer.step2Body: File → Export → Export plate sliced file into the watched folder — imported the same way, and the resulting .gcode.3mf gets the Send-to-printer button (Queue + Files tab).
settingsSlicer.profilesBody: Import the slicer sidecar's bundled Bambu printer, process and filament presets (version {{version}}). Edited or imported profiles are never overwritten.
settingsSlicer.pollingOff: Watched-folder polling is off — set a poll interval under Settings → General → Automation.
settingsSlicer.watchedFolderHint: That's the path inside the container — it maps to WATCH_HOST_DIR on the host.
settingsSlicer.copyNow: Copy it now — it won't be shown again. Set it as INTAKE_TOKEN in the post-processing script's environment.

settingsStorage.deleteDesc: This only removes the backend's configuration -- it never deletes files. The default backend, the last remaining backend, or one still holding files can't be deleted this way.
settingsStorage.title: Storage backends
settingsStorage.description: Run more than one backend at once -- the default is where new files are written; others can hold moved or replicated files.
